items.title: PAD: Policy-Aware Data Valuation for Autonomous Driving
items.snippet: End-to-end autonomous driving increasingly depends on scaling training demonstrations, yet data growth does not guarantee proportional gains. However, additional data do not guarantee better policies: a demonstration that benefits one planner may be redundant or harmful to another. Existing curation methods typically infer data value from intrinsic sample properties or training-dependent proxies that do not measure downstream policy utility. To address this, we introduce Policy-Aware Data Valuation (PAD), a framework that assigns each candidate demonstration a utility specific to the target driving policy. PAD combines scene-level calibration feedback with projected policy gradients and a re
items.title_ar: PAD: تقييم البيانات حسب سياسة القيادة الذاتية
items.summary_ar: ورقة بحثية تقدم PAD، وهو إطار يمنح كل demonstration للتدريب قيمة مرتبطة بسياسة القيادة الذاتية المستهدفة. يجمع الإطار بين calibration feedback و projected policy gradients لقياس المنفعة الفعلية للبيانات.
items.why_ar: فكرة data valuation حسب أداء النموذج النهائي قابلة للنقل إلى مشاريع تحسين بيانات التدريب في البنك.
items.title_en: PAD: Policy-Aware Data Valuation for Autonomous Driving
items.summary_en: This paper introduces PAD, a framework that assigns each candidate demonstration a utility specific to the target driving policy. It combines scene-level calibration feedback with projected policy gradients to measure downstream usefulness instead of intrinsic sample properties.
items.why_en: Its policy-aware data valuation idea can transfer to curating training data for models in a bank.

items.title: Muru
items.snippet: Muru Graham Dumpleton started mod_wsgi 20 years ago, and has been thinking about the ideal way to serve Python web applications in production ever since. Muru is his new, AI-assisted Rust server that aims to provide the best possible tools for running ASGI and WSGI Python apps both in development and production. As he did with wrapture , he's been publishing an extraordinarily detailed account of the project as he works on it - as part of his development process. Here's everything he's published

items.title: Squoosh Bench: Evaluating UX-1 on 318 Historical Website A/B Tests
items.snippet: Experimentation teams must decide which proposed website changes to test with live traffic. We evaluated whether forecasts from simulated shoppers could inform that choice. We screened 412 historical website A/B tests and evaluated four systems on the 318 that ran longer than 21 days. Each system predicted an original win, a variant win, or an inconclusive result. Page roles were masked and recorded outcomes were withheld during inference. Squoosh UX-1, a model fine-tuned on human browsing data, simulated 1,000 shoppers per arm and correctly classified 267 of 318 outcomes (84.0%, 95% Wilson interval 79.5-87.6%, treating experiments as independent). items.title_ar: Squoosh Bench: تقييم UX-1 على 318 تجربة A/B تاريخية
items.summary_ar: يقيّم بحث Squoosh Bench قدرة نموذج Squoosh UX-1، المدرّب على بيانات browsing بشرية، على التنبؤ بنتائج تجارب A/B تاريخية على مواقع الويب. يحاكي النموذج 1,000 مستخدم لكل نسخة ويصنّف النتيجة إلى فوز للنسخة الأصلية أو فوز للنسخة البديلة أو نتيجة غير حاسمة. حقق النموذج دقة 84.0% على 318 تجربة، وقورن بأنظمة أخرى منها Qwen3 Next 80B.
items.why_ar: يهمك لأنه يوضح إمكانية استخدام simulated shoppers للتنبؤ بنتائج التجارب قبل تشغيلها على traffic حقيقي.
items.title_en: Squoosh Bench: Evaluating UX-1 on 318 Historical A/B Tests
items.summary_en: Squoosh Bench evaluates whether Squoosh UX-1, a model fine-tuned on human browsing data, can forecast outcomes of 318 historical website A/B tests. The model simulates 1,000 shoppers per arm and classifies each test as original win, variant win, or inconclusive. It reached 84.0% accuracy and was compared against other systems including Qwen3 Next 80B.
items.why_en: It shows whether simulated shoppers can pre-screen website experiments before they consume live traffic.

items.title: Lang-SVG: Hierarchical Image Vectorization with Language Priors
items.snippet: Image vectorization reconstructs raster images as compact scalable vector graph- ics (SVG), providing a structured and editable code representation of images. However, most existing vectorization methods optimize for pixel-level render- ing fidelity, often producing SVGs that lack alignment with human-perceived object-part hierarchies, making them difficult to manipulate. To address this, we propose Lang-SVG, which introduces an explicit tree structure to organize SVG primitives with semantic labels and parent-child relationships. Lang-SVG incorporates granularity-controllable and open-vocabulary segmentation priors to initialize object-part hierarchies and leverages multimodal large languag
items.title_ar: Lang-SVG: تحويل الصور إلى SVG بهيكل هرمي بمساعدة اللغة
items.summary_ar: يقدم بحث Lang-SVG طريقة لتحويل الصور raster إلى SVG منظم كشجرة تحتوي على تسميات دلالية وعلاقات أب-ابن بين الأجزاء. تستخدم الطريقة segmentation مفتوحة المفردات وmultimodal large language models لتهيئة الهيكل الهرمي للكائنات والأجزاء.
items.why_ar: مفيد إذا كنت تعمل على multimodal models أو على استخراج بنى منظمة وقابلة للتحرير من الصور.
items.title_en: Lang-SVG: Hierarchical Image Vectorization with Language Priors
items.summary_en: Lang-SVG converts raster images into structured SVG organized as a tree with semantic labels and parent-child relations. It uses granularity-controllable, open-vocabulary segmentation priors and multimodal large language models to initialize object-part hierarchies.
items.why_en: It is relevant if you work on multimodal models or on turning images into editable structured representations.
